record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes a permanent weight edit using a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction and reports refusal and benign-answer outcomes. It does not report the original activation-projection and addition experiments.
record.gate_note: The README says abliterate.py prints before/after refusal rates, but gives no numeric results for that script in the text. The reported refusal and on-topic-answer figures concern the optional DPO-healed model. The README also describes candidate-layer selection and probe-based tuning, but those selection values are not reported as results.
record.test_reason: The repo applies the difference-in-means weight edit to a released model not in the original paper, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. Its README reports the behaviour itself, a refusal rate on held-out prompts, after the edit. That bears on V2 and on the ablation half of V1. The evidence is thin: README-only, with no counts, no original-model baseline and no judge details.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README presents abliteration as removing refusal through a weight edit. It says the edit usually costs some general quality and that optional DPO healing recovers it. On the default model, refusals stay at 0 and on-topic answers rise from 78% to 97% after healing. It also cautions that not refusing is not the same as answering well.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the harmful-minus-harmless difference in means, but implements it as a permanent orthogonalising weight edit rather than activation projection; README describes optional DPO healing. This is a tool repository, not a stated replication with reported reproduction results.
record.method_sensitivity: The README describes candidate layers at 40–80% depth and says the winning layer and edit strength are selected using probes; it does not report how outcomes vary across those settings.
record.problems: README-only evidence: evaluation prompt counts, judging details, uncertainty, and numeric refusal results for the unhealed edit are not stated. The answer-quality figure is after DPO healing, so it does not establish capability retention from the edit alone.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results were reported in the README. The script's stated before/after refusal-rate output is described as something it prints, but no values are included.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; activation-level ablation; broad capability benchmarks.
Models other than the default Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct; the README claims other architectures work but reports no results for them.

missing.what: The original model's refusal rate and on-topic answer rate before the edit. abliterate.py prints them, but the README gives no values.
Any results on the XSTest safe prompts (data/xstest_safe.csv) or from probe_refusal_split.py. Both files are listed, but no results for them are reported.

record.verdict_notes: This is a tool repo with README-only evidence; the code was not read. No uncertainty, prompt counts or judge details are given. The refusal tag is a phrase match. The verdicts are weak and rest on a single sentence of the README.

versions.untested_parts: No activation projection at every layer and position, no addition/steering experiment, and no broad general-capability evaluation are reported. The outcomes stated are for a permanent weight edit, with the answer-quality figure after DPO healing.
The README reports a result for the default Qwen model, not results across multiple released models; the unhealed edit's numeric refusal rate is not stated.
No jailbreak suppression or training-against-ablation robustness result is reported.
No comparison of one direction with multiple directions, a cone, or an affine description is reported.
No separate harmfulness-judgment and refusal-decision measurement is reported.
No language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer results are reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is reported.

rows.subject: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Abliterate with a permanent orthogonalising weight edit, then optionally DPO-heal; README says refusals stay at 0 after healing.
rows.note: The README reports that refusals stay at 0 on this model after optional healing. It does not give a numeric rate for the unhealed edit.
rows.check: "Refusals stay at 0" after healing implies the unhealed edit also gave 0 refusals, so the row should cover the edited model, not only the healed checkpoint. The baseline (the original model's refusal rate) is not stated, and the held-out prompt count is unknown. Refusal is detected by phrase match (stated for chat.py). The layer and strength were selected to remove every probe refusal, but the eval set is said to be separate.

rows.note: The README attributes the increase to healing and says the edit had cost answer quality. It does not specify the evaluation protocol or show that broader capabilities were preserved.
rows.check: The 78% baseline is the abliterated, unhealed model, not the original model. The 97% measures the effect of DPO healing, a separate intervention, not the ablation. tranche.reason: It uses the same diff-in-means direction and a weight orthogonalisation close to the original's. It applies them to a model the original did not use (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct) and reports a refusal rate after the edit. The original paper also did a weight edit, so the reader's earlier T2 fits less well.

statements.correction: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, diff-in-means orthogonalising weight edit (alpha walked down to weakest strength removing all probe refusals). README: refusals 0 after the edit and still 0 after optional DPO healing. On-topic answers 78% -> 97% after healing. No original-model refusal rate, prompt count or refusal detector given. README-only claim.
statements.problem: The statement correctly gives 0 refusals after DPO healing, but leaves out that 'stay at 0' implies the unhealed weight edit was also 0. For a residual-refusal comparison across weight edits, the edit itself is the comparable condition.
